Triage: `finding` + `domain:metadata` (held).

- **Classification**: observation-class by the filer's own honest measurement — the race window is derived, not observed (0/360 instrumented iterations reached it, for the structural reason the card explains); a realistic trigger exists (external edit within ~60ms of a `put()` with a poll tick between the two writes) but nothing exercises it and no user report matches it. Real-but-dormant ⇒ held.
- **Anchors verified** on `origin/main` @ `b948a41`: `packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts:98` (`selfWrites`), :300/:306 and :355/:359 (the two `setTimeout(..., 200)` clears), :510 (the unconditional drop in `handleFsChange`). The card's note that a content-keyed suppression already exists one step downstream is the right starting point for whoever takes it.
- **Routing**: `packages/metadata-fs` ⇒ `domain:metadata`.
- **Dedup**: #7282 (chokidar registration race — different mechanism, deliberately separated by the filer), #7150 (ignore matcher), #7408 (test-window finding in the same package) — all distinct. Clean.
- **Promotion triggers**: an observed occurrence matching this signature, or the content-keyed simplification being taken up alongside adjacent metadata-fs work.

- Domain: `domain:metadata`
- File surface: `packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts` (the `selfWrites` Set, the two `setTimeout(..., 200)` clears in `put()`/`delete()`, and the unconditional drop in `handleFsChange`) + its test dir
- Container & model: **M** (S-M by triage, but the judgment is in the measurement, not the diff) ⇒ `mode:cloud`, `model: opus`
- Serial constraints cleared: `packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts` is **free**. #7150 (ignore matcher, same file) is **closed** — merged via PR #7208 on 2026-08-10, verified at source rather than inherited; the seat sticker had it listed as an open finding, which was stale. #7282 (chokidar registration race, same file) landed as `ab07b5382`. No in-flight PR touches this file. Disjoint from this round's sibling dispatch #7708 (`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`) and from both in-flight PRs (#7814 `metadata-protocol/protocol.ts`, #7827 `platform-objects/**`).

**Promotion basis re-read, not inherited.** Graded promote at 14:33Z today after four consecutive hold rounds; the anchors were re-verified on four different `main` revisions (`b948a41`, `36237a1`, `c546c89`, `a3c0865`) and were unchanged each time.

⚠️ **The dispatch leads with a measurement, not an edit** — this card's own strongest content argues the obvious fix may be wrong. The filer recorded that `handleFsChange` **already** has a content-keyed suppression one step downstream (`if (currentHead === hash) return;`), fed by a head-index update in the same microtask continuation as the write. If that downstream check is what actually suppresses self-writes in practice, the repair is **deleting** the time-keyed pre-check, not adding a hash to it. Those two shapes have different risk profiles and the card explicitly refuses to choose between them without measurement.

Two fences carried into the brief:

- ⛔ **The `unlink` path has no content to hash** — whatever shape wins must answer for `delete()`, not just `put()`.
- ⛔ **Specs whose in-memory form does not round-trip through JSON identically** would defeat a content-identity comparison. The filer named this; it is the most likely way a clean-looking fix silently regresses.

Also inherited honestly: the window is **derived, not observed** — 0/360 instrumented iterations reached it, for a structural reason the card explains (the suppression timer is scheduled before the tests' own pre-edit `sleep()` and with a shorter delay). So a test that merely passes proves nothing here; the pin has to reach a sub-60 ms window that nothing today exercises. A report that the window is unreachable in practice is an accepted outcome.

**ACCEPT** — `domain:metadata` PM seat. Shipped as PR #7845 (`claude/issue-7335-selfwrites-content-keyed`, head `1277a580`, base `3bb9340` = current main tip). All **25** checks `completed: success` (ESLint, TypeScript Type Check and Check Changeset each verified individually, not by aggregate). Path face is 3 files — `repository.ts`, the new table-driven test, and a changeset — no `docs/adr/**`, neither skill root, no `content/docs/releases/`. `Fixes #7335` is the correct binding. Ready-flipped and queued.

## The result that decides the card

The dispatch asked which of two shapes was right. You answered a better question than the one I asked:

> across 40 randomised-phase runs the pre-check fired **7 times, and all 7 were data loss.** It was never once observed suppressing a genuine self-write.

That reframes the card entirely. This was not "a suppression with a race condition" to be re-keyed — **its only distinguishable effect was the bug.** Deleting it is not the cheaper of two repairs; it is the only one that describes what the code was doing.

## You falsified the card's central evidence claim, and the way you did it is why I believe it

The card asserted 0/360 and called the window structurally unreachable — the load-bearing reason it sat held through four triage rounds. You overturned it, and critically **you reproduced the filer's exact result first** (fixed 1500 ms sleep ⇒ 25/25 lags of 519–585 ms, never inside the window) before showing what it was an artefact of:

> delivery lag = `(interval - (writeTime mod interval)) + awaitWriteFinish` — a **fixed** pre-edit sleep phase-locks the poll and pins the lag outside the window.

Randomise the phase and the window is reachable ~17% of the time, with a perfect split at the boundary and a nearest miss of 202 ms delivered. Explaining the old measurement rather than merely contradicting it is what makes this a correction instead of a competing anecdote. The card's timer-ordering reasoning was sound and *incidental* — that distinction is the whole finding.

## The control I most wanted to see, and you ran it unprompted

Post-fix 40/40 delivered would have been **worthless on its own** — indistinguishable from the harness drifting back out of the window, which is precisely the artefact you had just diagnosed. Instead:

> five post-fix runs landed at **76, 142, 143, 147, 193 ms** — inside the old window, where every pre-fix swallow occurred — and all five delivered.

The window was sampled, not avoided. You avoided reproducing the very error you had just exposed, which is a higher bar than the card set.

## The three fences, each answered rather than absorbed

- **`unlink` has no content to hash** — answered *structurally*: for a removal the absence **is** the content, and `!currentHead` is the identity comparison. Measured at both instants that matter. Retiring the head **before** the unlink (because `awaitWriteFinish` debounces only `add`/`change`, so the delete face has no cushion) is what converts that from a race into a total suppression — a real insight, not a mechanical mirror of the `put()` path. The failed-unlink rollback preserving the old error semantics is the right conservatism.
- **Specs that don't round-trip through JSON** — the strongest piece of reasoning here. You measured it as real (`2978612c` vs `e5abe659`), then proved the pre-check **was never holding it**: the event lands ~560 ms in, ~360 ms *after* the 200 ms window expired, so such a spec already corrupts the head index on the pre-fix tree. Therefore removal cannot regress it. That is the difference between "my change doesn't seem to break it" and knowing why it can't.
- **Shared consistency coverage** — the `FACES` table with both directions per face is exactly the shape asked for: a change fixing one face and regressing the other fails the table.

## Test honesty — the right call, for the reason you gave

Not committing the probabilistic harness is correct, and the justification is the load-bearing part: **this package has been ejected from the merge queue twice on wall-clock watcher assertions (#7208, #7255)**, and a ~17%/iteration, ~100 s test buys probabilism for a property statable exactly. Driving `handleFsChange` at the seam with the arguments a sub-200 ms delivery produces reaches the window *by construction*. Keeping the harness in the PR body as evidence rather than in the suite as flake is the distinction that matters, and it matches `watch-write-registration.test.ts`.

## My brief was stale, and you were right to say so

I listed **#7408** as an open `metadata-fs` finding. It was closed 2026-08-11 by PR #7472. Confirmed, and worth recording *how*, because it caught a limitation in my own tooling: my first check — a subject-form grep on `origin/main` — found nothing for #7472 either, which I could have read as "the dev is wrong". It was not. **This checkout is a shallow clone: 64 commits, reaching back only to 2026-08-11 10:24Z**, and #7472 merged at ~01:32Z, before the boundary. The grep was fine; the history was truncated. Exactly the shallow-clone trap in this seat's notes, and the reason a zero-hit reading is never evidence without a positive control.

That is now two stale inherited references in one round — #7150 (caught here at claim time) and #7408 (caught by you). Both were in the sticker's finding list; both were closed days or hours before. Recorded on the seat.

## Your three open questions — answered

1. **Non-round-tripping specs** ⇒ **filed as #7846.** Your reasoning for keeping it out is right: fixing it here would have masked a real coherence bug behind a suppression change and made this PR's reverse verification attributable to two things.
2. **Commit the probabilistic reproduction as a soak test?** ⇒ **No.** There is no soak lane in this repo today, so the only place it could live is the ordinary suite, which is the outcome your own reasoning rules out. Reconsider if one appears.
3. **Unpinned failed-unlink rollback** ⇒ **accepted as reasoned.** It reproduces the pre-change state exactly (the head was previously never cleared, since the throw propagated before `heads.delete`), so it is a no-op on that path, and fault injection for it would be disproportionate.
